races.name: Close Brothers Asset Finance Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Pride Of Nepal
runners_data.note: Five wins from his last six starts including a course win, strong closing form at 10-12f on Good ground suits perfectly, but needs something to chase — if Harlington is truly uncontested this hold-up type faces the same wall of stopped horses as everyone else in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: Harlington
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here and the entire race shape bends around him; a habit of winning in front at 10f on Good is encouraging, though the step to 12f is untested and he has drifted from his winning form in his last three, so sustaining the effort to the line is the key question.

runners_data.name: Imperial Cult
runners_data.note: Trainer George Baker without a win in his last six runners is a note of caution, but Imperial Cult's two recent wins at 11-12f on Standard ground suggest he handles a genuinely-run pace well enough to be dangerous from just behind the leader; prominent profile suits this scenario perfectly.

runners_data.name: King's Castle
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with five place efforts from eight runs on Good going — consistent but hard to win — and the three-pound claimer Taryn Langley adds intrigue; trainer David Simcock has not had a winner in 14 days, and 40 days off is a minor fitness query, though King's Castle's record fresh is not alarming.

runners_data.name: Golden Phase
runners_data.note: Came off a 232-day absence and a string of shorter-course runs on Standard; genuinely wants to race prominently but is pushed back into midfield here by pace competition ahead — his chance is partially discounted because he is unlikely to get the prominent berth his form demands.

runners_data.name: Symphony's Song
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old stepping up from 7-8f and facing older, more experienced rivals; form figures of 4-6-4-5 are unencouraging and the trip is a big unknown, though if he gets a soft lead into the straight his stamina reserves have not been truly tested yet.

runners_data.name: Mrembo
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good at Sandown which is directly relevant course-and-distance form, and the headgear-wearing angle is worth noting; however, his true running style is a hold-up closer who has been mapped to midfield here simply because the field is packed at the rear — he will not naturally secure that forward position, which tempers expectations.

races.paceDynamic: Harlington is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this mile-and-two-furlong trip at Sandown. Imperial Cult and King's Castle will press from prominent positions, but neither is likely to force a truly searching gallop, meaning Harlington dictates on his own terms. This field does contain more prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate — Golden Phase is a natural front-runner who will be squeezed into midfield by the pace competition ahead, and Mrembo is a true hold-up type who may find more horses ahead of them than expected. A measured, front-led gallop that does not truly quicken until the home straight favours horses who can sit handy and travel smoothly, making the prominent-to-midfield profiles best placed, while genuine hold-up closers face an uphill task if the pace is never truly severe.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Harlington Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Harlington leads at his own pace and the field settles into a single-file, uncontested procession with no rival forcing a tempo increase.
scenarios.body: Harlington dictates every fraction, the moderate gallop compresses the field entering the straight, and horses who are handily placed can produce their effort without needing to make up ground; prominent sitters who travel fluidly are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Run On
scenarios.trigger: If Harlington's lead is sustainable but King's Castle or Imperial Cult track him tightly enough to wear him down in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: A controlled tempo still means no flood of finishing speed from the back, so the second and third horses in the group are best equipped to pass a tiring leader; this rewards patient prominent racers who conserve energy through the middle stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong enough to string the field out and create enough of a gap for a late charger to pick through tired rivals.
scenarios.body: Pride Of Nepal, who has won five of his last six starts and carries consistent closing form, is best positioned among the genuine hold-up types to benefit if the tempo is stronger than expected; Symphony's Song is too lightly exposed at this trip but gets a slim mention.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Phase or Mrembo manage to secure an uncharacteristically forward position early and use it to outstay the field.
scenarios.body: Both horses are natural prominent or hold-up types squeezed out of their preferred berths by the pace-heavy draw ahead of them, and their STYLE_FIT discounts make this shape the least likely to reward them; if either does find a good spot by luck of the draw or a slow early pace, their course-and-distance form gives them a residual chance.

watchPoints.text: Watch Harlington's early fractions — if he goes too slow the field bunches and his lead is worthless, but if he goes too fast he risks stopping in the Sandown straight before the mile-and-two is complete.
Golden Phase has a 232-day layoff; monitor market moves closer to post time as a significant drift could indicate he is not fully wound up and his out-of-role position makes the risk compounded.

Pride Of Nepal carries top weight at 138lbs alongside Harlington and Imperial Cult — weight compression at the top of the handicap could blunt his finishing kick if the pace is anything less than genuine.

Symphony's Song and Mrembo both have apprentice jockeys with 3-7lb claims; in a compressed, pace-controlled race, positional errors from less-experienced riders could cost either horse a clean run through the straight at Sandown's tight home turn.

races.name: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Close Brothers Premium Finance Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Appier
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist for Tony Carroll with solid placed form at 14f–18f; sim-going record on good is concerning (0W0P from 15 runs) and this trip is a touch short of their best stamina range at 1m6f — watch for late run that may not quite reach the leaders.

runners_data.name: Personal Best
runners_data.note: Front-runner operating at a STYLE_FIT of 0.92, which tempers confidence despite leading; Jason Watson's booking is positive and five placed finishes from five good-ground runs show consistency, but this horse has yet to convert — the uncontested lead is the big enabler here.

runners_data.name: Knight Templar
runners_data.note: Robert Stephens runner returning after 121 days off, but has won twice at 1m6f on good/standard and placed twice more — the distance-going-course profile is the standout in this field; David Probert's ride and the proximity to Personal Best will be key, and the absence is the only genuine doubt.

runners_data.name: Ludo's Landing
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner sports blinkers and has a win over 12f on standard ground, but the recent form includes a good-ground fifth and eleventh, and the sim-going figures (1W3P from 15) suggest this trip and surface combination is workable rather than ideal — the headgear may sharpen focus.

runners_data.name: Laravie
runners_data.note: Laravie arrives in excellent winning form (four wins from last five, six wins from 11 on good ground) and is James Owen's flagbearer here; a genuine prominent racer, they are structurally bumped back to midfield by the field's configuration, which means Luke Morris must navigate traffic rather than dictate — visor retained, and the form demands respect regardless.

runners_data.name: Mister Daydream
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's five-year-old is back just 11 days after last run, bringing consecutive wins at 10f–12f on standard; the step up to 1m6f is a clear stamina query, and although their true hold-up style is shown in midfield due to redistribution, Rhys Clutterbuck will need this longer trip to suit before any late challenge can land.

races.paceDynamic: Personal Best is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only six runners over 1m6f on good ground, is likely to dictate at a controlled, unhurried gallop with no genuine rival to press them into a faster tempo. Knight Templar has prominent tendencies and may sit just behind, but neither they nor anyone else in this small field is wired to chase Personal Best down early, meaning the pace is likely to be steady rather than searching. Laravie is a natural prominent type with a sharp recent winning sequence but is redistributed to midfield because Personal Best and Knight Templar fill the front positions first; Mister Daydream is a genuine hold-up horse but is also mapped to midfield for similar structural reasons, meaning neither is operating in their truest zone. A sustainable, front-controlled gallop over this stamina trip strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and quicken off a modest pace — pure closers will find the race not run to suit, as a slow early tempo compresses the finish and rewards those with positional priority.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Personal Best Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Personal Best dictates an uncontested lead and kicks clear in the straight unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Personal Best takes full advantage of the soft tempo, setting their own fractions and finding the 1m6f trip perfectly suited to an uncontested front-running display; at OR=79 with recent placed form on good ground, this is a textbook scenario for a horse allowed to bowl along in front. Knight Templar, already primed to sit close to the pace after 121 days off, is positioned to capitalise if Personal Best weakens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Knight Templar travels strongly close to Personal Best and challenges emphatically from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Knight Templar has won over this course and distance combination on good ground and, with David Probert riding, is capable of tracking Personal Best into a strong finish from an ideal position; the 121-day absence is the key uncertainty, but the trainer's form and distance record support this outcome. Laravie, despite being shuffled back from their natural prominent slot, has six wins from 11 outings on good ground at similar trips and could still pick up the pieces if the front two fight each other into the ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than anticipated and the field strings out, creating a true stamina test.
scenarios.body: Appier has winning form over comparable trips on soft-of-firm ground and Neil Callan can angle them wide for a clear run if the field tires; Ludo's Landing has a win over 12f on soft and placed form at 13f on good, so if the stamina emphasis sharpens, they stay on best of all. However, this scenario depends on a genuine gallop that this small field is unlikely to generate, making it a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Personal Best is outrun early or fades badly, causing a scrambled finish with no clear beneficiary.
scenarios.body: Should Personal Best fail to sustain their lead into the straight, the field bunches and the race becomes a sprint finish off a falsely slow pace, which theoretically suits Laravie's form profile given six wins from 11 good-ground outings — though they are not in their natural position here. Mister Daydream, a genuine hold-up type with back-to-back wins and quick return to action, has the raw ability to capitalise in a muddled closing surge.

watchPoints.text: Personal Best's front-running platform is the race's defining factor — if they are pressured even minimally off the break by Knight Templar or Laravie, the entire pace map changes and the race becomes genuinely open.

Knight Templar's 121-day absence is the single biggest form unknown in the race; if they return fit and sharp, David Probert is ideally placed to track Personal Best and strike, but fitness questions make this a watch rather than a certainty.

Laravie's redistribution to midfield is a material concern — Luke Morris must ride against the horse's natural instincts, and if they get blocked or fail to find clear daylight at the 2f pole, a winning run of form could be broken by pure positional misfortune.

Mister Daydream's 11-day turnaround and significant step up in trip from 12f to 1m6f should be monitored in the betting market and pre-race inspection — a quick return is not unusual for this yard but the distance jump is a legitimate stamina flag.

races.name: Close Brothers Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Cyrano De Bergerac
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's lightly-raced three-year-old has won over 10f in good going and finished placed in his last two, making him the most straightforwardly well-suited runner to today's conditions — prominent style meshes cleanly with the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Hot And Cold
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott has this horse in fine form after back-to-back wins, but both came over 8f and the step up to 1m2f is uncharted territory; the solo-lead role is straightforward but stamina must be proven, and the style-fit flag tempers confidence in it fully executing.

runners_data.name: Knightsail
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's hold-up type is 107 days absent and fitted with a hood, and while it placed at Goodwood over 9f in good going, the lack of pace in this small field is an awkward fit for Jamie Spencer's waiting tactics — needs more gallop than this race is likely to provide.

runners_data.name: Blue Noon
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's runner has been consistently placed at this trip on good ground and the unknown style tag reflects some tactical flexibility, but four runs without a win this season and a trainer 14-day strike of 7/56 suggest modest expectations; likely to travel well without necessarily finding a decisive turn of foot.

runners_data.name: Roker Roar
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding has a good 14-day strike rate (13/54) but this hold-up type has been off 184 days, has never run on good ground with success, and steps into territory where the absence of genuine pace pressure makes a late run from off the back very difficult to execute.

races.paceDynamic: Hot And Cold is the lone confirmed front-runner here, though tagged with a style-fit discount as a horse racing somewhat out of its natural role stepping up markedly in trip to 1m2f having won over 8f. With no genuine challenger for the lead, Hot And Cold will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front, unlikely to be pressured at any stage by Cyrano De Bergerac (prominent) or the hold-up pair of Knightsail and Roker Roar. Blue Noon's style is uncertain but has raced prominently in the past and may track Hot And Cold into second position, giving the race a fairly compressed, sedate early pace. A steady, uncontested lead with no pace injection until the straight suits horses with tactical versatility who can travel close to the pace and quicken from a position of comfort — making the prominent and close-tracking profiles the primary beneficiaries, while true hold-up types face an uncomfortable test if the gallop never genuinely stretches.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Hot And Cold dictates a steady, uncontested pace and the race is decided on finishing kicks from close to the front.
scenarios.body: Hot And Cold sets fractions that suit those tracking it, and a prominent runner like Cyrano De Bergerac — who has won over the trip in good going and is improving at three — is ideally positioned to pounce turning in. The steady gallop rewards horses who can travel economically close to the pace rather than those asked to make up significant ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely stronger than expected and the front two tie each other up, leaving a gap for a late closer.
scenarios.body: Knightsail, who placed at Goodwood over the trip in good going, would be the primary beneficiary if there is enough pace to bring stamina into play on the run-in. Roker Roar is 184 days off the track and unproven on this going combination, making Knightsail the more likely hold-up winner in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Blue Noon Tracks Through
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Noon settles into a prominent position behind Hot And Cold and produces a sustained run to catch the leader.
scenarios.body: Blue Noon has finished third in good going at this trip multiple times and is consistent if not spectacular, and a slow pace that compresses the field could suit his ability to travel and grind. Richard Hannon's runner has the course and distance form, though the low strike-rate over 14 days is a mild concern.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Hot And Cold, freed from pressure, sets a deceptively strong gallop that drains the field before the home turn.
scenarios.body: Despite the step up in trip and the style-fit concern, Sir Mark Prescott horses are notoriously well-prepared and Hot And Cold's two consecutive wins suggest it is in a rich vein of form. If connections have specifically schooled this horse for the longer trip, a wire-to-wire victory on a sustainable lead is not impossible.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Hot And Cold settles comfortably in front over this 1m2f trip — any sign of pulling hard or racing keenly early would be significant given the unproven stamina.
Knightsail's hood and 107-day absence are worth monitoring at the start; if it misses the break or dwells, Jamie Spencer's hold-up tactics become unworkable with only five runners.
Blue Noon's position in the first two furlongs is key — if it sits prominently behind Hot And Cold, it becomes a live contender; if it drops away to the rear, its chance diminishes sharply.
Roker Roar's 184-day layoff means its fitness level is the biggest unknown in the race; watch its market moves for any late confidence from the Balding yard before drawing conclusions.

races.name: Close Brothers Invoice Finance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Winston's Warrior
runners_data.note: Charles Hills has this horse in good form (two wins this season) and he has strong course form over this mile; the concern is a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he is racing out of his natural role, and his recent prominent tag may mean he ends up conceding ground at the start rather than commanding the front as he ideally would.|

runners_data.name: Cristo
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner with a strong record over this course and distance in similar going, including a win and multiple placings over Sandown's mile; Sean Levey takes the ride and he has won here before, giving Cristo a formidable jockey-course-trainer combination that makes him a key player across most scenarios.|

runners_data.name: Sea Suite
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by James Owen, fitted with a visor and wearing headgear that may sharpen his response to pressure; has a win and two placings over similar ground and trip, and Luke Morris gives him an experienced pilot — the key question is whether the pace is sufficient for him to close from the rear given Winston's Warrior's controlled tempo.|

runners_data.name: Bubbles Wonky
runners_data.note: Mark Pattinson's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose true style has been mapped to midfield here because the rear of the field is overcrowded; 65 days since last run is a notable freshness concern, and all five recent runs have come on Tapeta at Wolverhampton, making this Good turf debut at Sandown a significant unknown.|

runners_data.name: Lorca's Waltz
runners_data.note: William Haggas three-year-old who carries a tongue tie and arrives fresh after 38 days off; only three career runs but one of those was a winning debut over this exact course and distance on Good ground, which is a compelling form pointer — Cieren Fallon rides and the yard is 4/46 in 14 days suggesting modest current form.|

runners_data.name: Swiped
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old has won twice over a mile on Good ground and twice placed, giving him a strong profile for this trip and surface; however, he is a genuine prominent racer who has been redistributed to midfield in the map because multiple horses seek that position, and the STYLE_FIT flag means his chance is tempered if he cannot secure his natural early berth — Rhys Clutterbuck takes over from a more experienced jockey.|

races.paceDynamic: Winston's Warrior is the sole confirmed front-runner here and looks set to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable, uncontested tempo over this mile at Sandown. Cristo and Swiped are both genuine prominent types who will want to race close to the pace, meaning the front rank will have company through the early stages even if no direct challenge to Winston's Warrior materialises immediately. That controlled, single-pace gallop set by Winston's Warrior favours horses who can travel in behind and produce a finish, making hold-up and midfield runners — particularly Lorca's Waltz and Sea Suite — the profiles best suited to this shape. This field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate at their natural positions; Swiped and Bubbles Wonky are genuine prominent and hold-up horses respectively who are likely to find themselves racing further back than they would prefer, with Cristo and Winston's Warrior best placed to secure their natural berths near the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Winston's Warrior sets an unhurried gallop and the pace stays honest without a sustained challenge from Cristo or Swiped.
scenarios.body: Winston's Warrior dictates from the front at a moderate tempo, setting up a test that rewards horses travelling smoothly in behind before producing a late kick; the Sandown mile's finishing straight places a premium on a strong, well-timed finish from midfield to rear. Lorca's Waltz and Sea Suite are the profiles that benefit most, with both capable of holding a position and unleashing a run if the pace is controlled and the tempo honest without being punishing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Winston's Warrior gets a soft lead and the tempo is slow enough that he conserves energy to deny challengers in the straight.
scenarios.body: With Cristo and Swiped unable to fully assert their natural prominent tendencies, Winston's Warrior dictates an economy-of-effort gallop that leaves him with enough in reserve to repel the finish of hold-up horses; Sandown's slightly stiff finish makes this scenario viable if the tempo is genuinely slow. Winston's Warrior is the direct beneficiary here, with Cristo best placed to chase if he can track efficiently from his prominent position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Assert
scenarios.trigger: If Cristo pushes forward to press Winston's Warrior and the pace quickens from an early stage, creating a more honest gallop.
scenarios.body: Cristo challenges for the lead or sits a close second, pushing the tempo higher and stretching the field, which can expose any hold-up horses who struggle to close a larger gap on fast ground at a mile; Sea Suite's hold-up style becomes a disadvantage if the pace is stronger and the gaps don't appear. Cristo is the major beneficiary here given his strong record at this course and distance, with Winston's Warrior also coping if the pace suits his stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Closers Denied
scenarios.trigger: If Swiped and Bubbles Wonky race out of their natural positions and disrupt the pace pattern, creating an uneven or falsely run contest.
scenarios.body: Redistributed runners Swiped and Bubbles Wonky failing to find their preferred spots introduces erratic pace variation, with gaps appearing and closing unpredictably and horses unable to deliver their usual finishing patterns; in this disrupted shape, the horses with tactical flexibility and experience over the course — Cristo and Winston's Warrior — are most likely to capitalise on positional advantages. True hold-up types like Bubbles Wonky and Sea Suite are the least likely to benefit in a race where pace flow is compromised by displacement from natural roles.

watchPoints.text: Winston's Warrior's ability to secure the front unchallenged is critical — if Cristo or Swiped push forward aggressively at the start, the pace lifts and Winston's Warrior's hold on the lead is compromised, reshaping the entire race.

Bubbles Wonky's 65-day absence combined with a move from Wolverhampton Tapeta to Good Sandown turf is a significant double-flag — watch the market and paddock closely for signs this runner is fit and adapting to the surface.

Swiped is a natural front-runner mapped to midfield due to congestion; if Clutterbuck elects to push forward regardless, it could create a contested early pace that undermines Winston's Warrior and opens the race up for hold-up types.

Lorca's Waltz's sole win came over this exact course, distance and going — that specificity of course form at Sandown is worth tracking in running to see whether Cieren Fallon positions him prominently enough to exploit a slow pace or whether he gets outpaced early.

Sea Suite's visor is first-time headgear in recent races — headgear changes at this level can produce significant improvement or prove ineffective; watch for how alertly he jumps and whether Luke Morris can place him in a position to strike from his hold-up berth.

races.name: Close Brothers Motor Finance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lyra Lea
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with good-going form over seven furlongs; Rod Millman's filly has placed at this trip and track condition before but her sim-going record is modest (4/10, no wins), and her STYLE_FIT flag suggests her listed prominent role here is actually slightly out of character — she is the race's pace anchor regardless.

runners_data.name: Decalogue
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's three-year-old has a worrying tendency to fade in the finish and has failed to place in any of his last three starts on standard and good ground; 58 days off the track adds a fitness query, and a true hold-up style over a trip that often punishes one-paced closers at Sandown makes this a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Unionville
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's gelding has strong form at six furlongs on standard ground (two wins in last five) but now steps up to seven furlongs on turf for the first time — the extra furlong is the key unknown, and a hold-up style means he needs a stronger pace than Lyra Lea is likely to provide.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Boom
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's colt has the most relevant profile in this race shape — prominent style, 1W2P from five runs on good going, and a win over seven furlongs on good ground; Jason Watson's booking and a T14 strike rate of 13/54 from a powerful yard underline its leading credentials in this particular scenario.

runners_data.name: Norfolk Blue
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon rides a horse that carries headgear (p) and is a genuine hold-up runner by nature — the map places him in midfield only because hold-up positions are overcrowded, not because he races there voluntarily; six runs on good and good-to-soft ground show 0W1P, and his STYLE_FIT flag reflects the positioning compromise he faces in this small field.

runners_data.name: King Cherry
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' gelding is wearing a tongue-tie and has been absent 70 days — the longest layoff in the field — with a form string of just 758 and no win or place on good ground; a true hold-up type squeezed into a mapped midfield slot by field composition, this horse needs significant improvement and better conditions to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Lyra Lea is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field and should lead uncontested from the outset over Sandown's 7f, setting a measured, sustainable gallop without any genuine pace pressure from rivals. Berkshire Boom is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely track Lyra Lea in second, meaning the two horses furthest forward dictate the entire tempo. The remainder — Decalogue, Unionville, Norfolk Blue, and King Cherry — are all hold-up types by nature, though Norfolk Blue and King Cherry have been redistributed to midfield in the map because the field carries more closers than can realistically occupy the rear; in practice, those two are true hold-up runners who may struggle to find their natural ground-saving position in a small, slowly-run field. With a single front-runner controlling pace and no credible challenger to push the tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the lead — the gallop is unlikely to be searingly fast, which will blunt the closing power of the genuine hold-up horses and reward those who travel in the first two or three positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lyra Lea Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lyra Lea bowls along in front at a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the pace-scenario plays out as projected.
scenarios.body: Lyra Lea sets a controlled tempo, Berkshire Boom tracks closely, and the hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up in the closing stages on Sandown's uphill finish; horses racing in the first two positions have a decisive positional advantage. Berkshire Boom's good-going record over this course-and-distance combination and prominent style make it the chief beneficiary if the leader tires late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Draw Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Lyra Lea and Berkshire Boom stride clear from the two-furlong pole and the closers simply cannot close the gap.
scenarios.body: The restrained gallop means neither front-runner has been over-extended, and the uphill Sandown finish favours those who have conserved energy in a forward position; the hold-up horses make ground but the deficit is too great. This scenario rewards Berkshire Boom in particular, given its proven win form on good ground at seven furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Lyra Lea goes too fast too soon or the pace is quicker than expected, opening the door for the genuine hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Decalogue or Unionville would need the front-runners to have set a strong enough gallop to leave them vulnerable in the final furlong on the climb; this is a low-probability shape given the absence of any pace-pressure. Note that Norfolk Blue and King Cherry, though true hold-up horses by nature, are mapped to midfield precisely because this field offers no natural pace to exploit — their redistribution further undermines this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Modest Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so slow it turns into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole, negating all pace analysis.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race scrambles positional advantages, but Berkshire Boom's tactical versatility and course form still give it an edge in a sprint; Lyra Lea's stamina is untested in a dash. This is a very unlikely shape given Lyra Lea's front-running confirmation.

watchPoints.text: Berkshire Boom — watch for Jason Watson to position him directly behind Lyra Lea from the off; if he gets that prominent sit in a race with no pace pressure, his good-going form over seven furlongs puts him in a very strong place turning for home.
Lyra Lea — if she jumps slowly or is slower than usual to establish her lead, Berkshire Boom could take the front and change the dynamic entirely, leaving Lyra Lea racing out of her natural position.

Norfolk Blue and King Cherry — both are genuine hold-up horses crowded into midfield roles by field composition; watch to see if Cieren Fallon or Marco Ghiani attempt to drop them back to their natural position regardless, which could leave them with significantly more ground to make up.

Unionville — stepping up in trip from six to seven furlongs on turf is an unproven combination for this horse; if the pace is steady and he is asked to finish from off the bridle, the stamina question will be answered publicly here for the first time.
